Stereoselective Iodolactonization of 4-Allenoic Acids with Efficient Chirality
Transfer: Development of a New Electrophilic Iodination Reagent
Xiaobing Zhang, [a] Chunling Fu, [a] Yihua Yu,[b] and Shengming Ma* [a]
Introduction
Electrophilic cyclization of 2-allenyl compounds with a nu-
cleophilic moiety at the 1-position has proved to be a power-
ful method for the synthesis of five-membered cyclic com-
pounds.
[1, 2] The intrinsic axial chirality of the allene moiety
permits enantioselective synthesis of optically active cyclic
products provided that chirality transfer may be realized
through an anti-cyclization mode. [3] However, with an elon-
gated carbon chain between the allene unit and the nucleo-
philic moiety (compounds 1; n > 2), in addition to the issues
of regioselectivity and axial chirality transfer, it is a chal-
lenge to control to the configuration of the remaining C =C
bond in products B, which are obtained through an exo-cyc-
lization mode (Scheme 1).
[4]
In 2007, we observed that the iodolactonization of ( R)-4-
allenoic acids 3 affords racemic ( Z)-5 by way of a cationic
mechanism, whereas electrophilic anti cyclization afforded
an inseparable mixture of ( S)-(Z)-5 and ( R)-(E)-5
(Scheme 2). It should be noted that the absolute configura-
tions in these two products are opposite. To make this type
of cyclization useful in organic synthesis, we must address

Abstract: A highly stereoselective iodolactonization of 4-allenoic acids with a new
sterically demanding electrophilic iodination reagent to afford optically active g-
butyrolactones has been developed. The reaction shows high efficiency of axial
chirality transfer and excellent Z/E selectivity and has been applied to the synthe-
sis of chiral cis-b,g-disubstituted g-butyrolactones to give very high diastereomeric
and enantiomeric excess values. The reaction has been successfully utilized in the
synthesis of naturally occurring compounds (
+)-cis-whisky lactone and ( +)-cis-3-
methyl-4-decanolide.

Results and Discussion
Cyclization to address Z/E selectivity and maintain high effi-
ciency for axial chirality transfer : To develop our new proto-
col, we used ( Ra)-3a with allene axial chirality as the model
substrate. As expected, albeit with much disappointment,
(S)-5-(1’-iodo-1’-(Z)-octenyl)-4,5-dihydro-2(3H)-furanone
[(S)-(Z)-5a ] and ( R)-5-(1’-iodo-1’-(E)-octenyl)-4,5-dihydro-
2(3H)-furanone [( R)-(E)-5a ] were obtained with a dia-
ACHTUNGTRENNUNGstereomeric ratio (d.r.) of 78:22, in 99 % yield when NIS ( 6;
2 equiv) was used, although there is no obvious racemization
(Table 1, entry 2).
It should be noted that the configuration of the remaining
C=C bond and the absolute configuration of the central chir-
ality in these two isomers are opposite to each other,
[4b]
which also results in an enantiomeric excess ( ee) of the
product of only 56 % after hydrogenation of the C =C bond
and reduction of the C /C0I bond. By consideration of the
nature of this iodolactonization reaction, we reasoned that a
more sterically demanding electrophilic iodination reagent,
such as 7 or 8, might provide a much-improved stereoselec-
tivity (Scheme 3).
First, when 7—with a benzene ring to replace the two
methylene units of 6—was prepared and used,
[5] the ratio of
(S)-(Z)-5a /(R)-(E)-5a was improved to 93:7 (Table 1,
entry 3). T o our delight, when 8—with a naphthalene ring
modification[6]—was used, the selectivity of ( S)-(Z)-5a /(R)-
(E)-5a was improved further to 97:3 (Table 1, entry 4).
Such a strategy is general for the highly stereoselective io-
dolactonization of 4-allenoic acids with axial chirality. The
efficiency of chirality transfer is very high, demonstrated by
the reactions of ( R
a)-3b, and ( Ra)-3c (Scheme 4 b). As ex-
pected, enantiomer ( R)-(Z)-5a may be prepared from ( Sa)-
3a (Scheme 4 a).
Application to the synthesis of thermodynamically unstable
b,g-disubstituted cis butyrolactones: We have previously re-
ported[4b, f] that the highly diastereoselective iodolactoniza-
tion of optically active 4-allenoic acids ( Ra,R)-3, via the in-
termediacy of p-allylic cationic species 9, led to the forma-
tion of thermodynamically more stable b,g-disubstituted
trans products by 1,2-chiral induction (Scheme 5). Therefore,
we envisioned that it may now be possible to synthesize the
relatively unstable b,g-disubstituted cis-g-butyrolactones
with high stereoselectivity, provided that the newly formed
chiral carbon center at the g-position is generated by chirali-

We were happy to see that chirality transfer is operational
for the synthesis of thermodynamically disfavored b,g-disub-
stituted cis butyrolactones; the reaction of ( Ra,R)-(/C0)-3d
with 8 afforded (4 R,5S)-5-(1’-iodo-1’-(Z)-butenyl)-4-methyl-
4,5-dihydro-2(3H)-furanone [(4 R,5S)-(Z)-5d ] in 70 % yield
with a E/Z ratio of > 97:3 (Table 2, entry 1). An allyl group
was also tolerated at the b position of the furanone, which
indicated a much higher reactivity of the allene moiety rela-
tive to the allylic C =C bond (Table 2, entries 3 and 4). Fur-
thermore, an R
1 substituent with larger steric hindrance,
such as an isopropyl group, could also be used in the reac-
tion and gave excellent selectivity (Table 2, entry 5).
To further illustrate the generality of this strategy, ( R)-3-
methyl-6-phenylhexa-4,5-dienoic acid [( R)-3h ] was prepared
by the chemistry shown in Scheme 6.
[4b] Compound (3 S,4S)-
3-methyl-4-ethynyloxetan-2-one [(3 S,4S)-11] was converted
to a 3-allenoic acid, followed by reduction with LiAlH 4 to
form alcohol ( Ra,S)-12. Tosylation and subsequent cyanation
afforded nitrile ( Ra,R)-13. Finally, hydrolysis with NaOH in
EtOH/H2O afforded the allenoic acid ( R)-3h . However, epi-
merization of the axial chirality of the allene moiety was ob-
served, which led to the formation of a pair of equal dia-
ACHTUNGTRENNUNGstereoisomers. When ( R)-3h was treated with 8 under the
standard conditions, (4 R,5R)-(Z)-5h was afforded as a single
isomer in 54 % yield. This result indicated that the reaction
proceeded through the intermediacy of p-allylic cationic
species 9, which led to the formation of the thermodynami-
cally more stable trans product by 1,2-chiral induction. [4b]
This is clearly caused by stabilization of the cationic inter-
mediate by the phenyl substituent.
Rationale for the observed stereoselectivity : It is in-
teresting to observe that in the absence of Cs 2CO3,
the reaction of ( Ra,R)-3d with 8 afforded a much
lower ratio (89:11) of (4 R,5S)-(Z)-5d /ACHTUNGTRENNUNG(4R,5R)-(Z)-
5d (Scheme 7), which indicates the unique effect of
the base on the stereoselectivity of this reaction.
Based on these facts, the high Z stereoselectivity
and efficiency of chirality transfer observed can be
rationalized as follows (Scheme 8). The reaction of
allenoic acid 3 with iodination reagent 8 would
afford iodonium intermediate ( Z)-14 or ( E)-14,i n
which the amide anion plays an important role (for-
mation of a hydrogen-bonded four-membered
unit)
[7] in determining the stereoselectivity by the
steric interaction with R 1.

[9] Thus, there are many reports devoted
to the synthesis of 15[10] and 16.[11] Fukuzawa et al., [10b] Proct-

ported the synthesis of 15, in which the chiral centers of the
target were constructed by the reaction of a chiral reagent
with a key intermediate to afford a pair of diastereoisomers,
which were separated by chromatography on silica gel; sub-
sequent transformations gave the target with 6.6 (nine steps)
and 6.2 % yield (six steps), respectively. For the synthesis of
16, Wu et al.
[11] reported a route from ( S)-N-propionyl-4-
benzyl-3-propanoyloxazolidin-2-one and heptanal in five
steps, with no ee value given. Kitahara et al. reported a syn-
thesis of 16 in eight steps from (1 S,5R)-2-oxabicycloACHTUNGTRENNUNG[3.3.0]-
oct-6-en-3-one, however, the yield was low (2 %), due to the
fact that two steps in this approach gave a larger number of
recovery.
[9] Syntheses of 15 and 16 from chiral auxiliaries
gave good yields but low d.r. and ee values,[10b–d] whereas
syntheses that gave good stereoselectivity of the target mol-
ecules were accompanied by low yields
[10e–f] and advanced
chiral starting materials [9, 11] were required. Therefore, devel-
opment of new efficient routes with higher stereoselectivi-
ties and yields, from simple starting materials, is still of in-
terest.
The synthetic application of our iodolactonization reac-
tion to short asymmetric syntheses of 15 and 16 was demon-
strated (Scheme 9). Both 15 and 16 were synthesized easily
in two steps, from (4 R,5S)-(Z)-5d (89 %) and (4 R,5S)-(Z)-
5e (93 %), respectively. Measured optical rotation and
1H
and 13C NMR analysis of the products were in good agree-
ment with previous reports. Compared to all of the known
routes, this process displays the highest diastereoselectivity
and ee for the final products.
[10, 11]
Conclusion
We have developed a highly stereoselective iodolactoniza-
tion of 4-allenoic acids, which proceeds via a three-mem-
bered iodonium ion intermediate to afford chiral g-butyro-
lactones, by development of a sterically demanding iodina-
tion reagent. The synthesis of b,g-disubstituted cis-g-butyro-
lactones from the starting materials with different steric
nature is especially noteworthy. This reaction has been suc-
cessfully applied to the synthesis of naturally occurring lac-
tones, (
+)-cis-whisky lactone and ( +)-cis-3-methyl-4-decano-
lide. Due to the high Z/E stereoselectivity, excellent efficien-
cy of chirality transfer, the substituent-loading capability of
the starting allenoic acids, and potential uses of the prod-
ucts, this reaction—in particular, the new iodination re-
agent—will be useful in organic chemistry, especially for the
synthesis of a series of naturally occurring cis-g-butyrolac-
tones.
[12] Further studies in this area are ongoing in our labo-
ratory.
